document.title: Afghanistan: Where We Stand and What We Need (Kabul 003863)
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), New Documents Detail America's Strategic Response to 9/11
document.note: [Secret] Neumann says 'we are not winning in Afghanistan; although we are far from losing.' Resources lag increasing Taliban offensives. He recommends equipping Afghan forces, taking out Taliban leadership in Pakistan, and investing in infrastructure; the Taliban believe they are winning, which 'scares the hell out of Afghans.'

events.description: Ambassador Neumann sends cable assessing that US is not winning but not losing and requesting resources.
Large Taliban offensive in the South, bigger than predicted.
Operation Mountain Thrust bought time, particularly in Oruzgan.
Planned visit of President Karzai to Washington.
NSA Rassoul visited Pakistani counterpart Aziz; presidents Karzai and Musharraf may meet.
Afghan NSA Rassoul visited his Pakistani counterpart Aziz.
Possible Karzai–Musharraf meeting under discussion; both sides seem ready.
Planned Karzai visit to Washington; embassy recommends announcing new funds and new visions for Afghan forces.
Ambassador Neumann's cable concludes that the US is not losing but is too slow; recommends $600 million supplemental and more local auxiliary police.
US/coalition braced for a Taliban offensive anticipated in February but were surprised by its size.
Mountain Thrust operation bought time, particularly in Oruzgan.
Large Taliban offensive in south with unexpected numbers of insurgents.
Planned Karzai visit to Washington, to announce programs for equipping Afghan security forces and road building.
Ambassador Neumann cable states 'We are not winning in Afghanistan' and requests resources, $600m roads.

key_claims: The US Ambassador judged in August 2006 that the coalition was not winning but not losing in Afghanistan.
The Taliban offensive in the south in 2006 was far larger than predicted, expanding their control of the rural population.
The Taliban's leadership is secure in Pakistan and believes it can prevail; the embassy wants Pakistan to take out Taliban leadership.
The south (Kandahar, Helmand, Ghazni) deteriorated while the east improved through military action, roads and better governors.
Poppy eradication in Helmand may have pushed drug lords and some tribal elements to back the Taliban.
The embassy sought $600 million for roads and accelerated ANSF equipping, to be announced around Karzai's 26 September Washington visit.
